title: message_template
description: The wording of one message for one channel and one audience, kept as data so the Console can edit it (see CMS_GUIDE.md and MESSAGE_TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md). One record per kind, channel and audience. The body is a list of blocks, not HTML: the channel turns the blocks into the text and HTML versions. Versions are linked records: a draft is edited in place; publishing turns the draft into the new published record, whose previous_id names the published record it replaces; the standing version is the published record nobody supersedes. Rules the schema cannot express: only a published and active record is ever sent; at most one draft and one standing published record per kind, channel and audience; every placeholder must name a fact the kind supplies, and a placeholder for an optional fact must sit inside a block or row guarded by that fact's show_if (the kind's fact schema decides, and the Console and check.py refuse anything else); curly braces are used only for placeholders; fields marked readOnly are set by the server only.
x_retention: Kept. Every published version stays so a log entry's template_version can be explained. (A written policy only; nothing enforces it yet.)

kind.description: The message kind this wording is for, such as placement_confirmation. Must be a kind registered in registry.json. Required.

channel.description: The channel this wording is for. Only email exists today; a short text-message version is added later as another record. Required.

audience.description: Which people get this wording, such as student or requester. Must be one of the audiences the kind lists. The caller names the audience; the CMS does not know what the word means. Required.

name.description: A plain-words name shown in the Console. Up to 120 characters. Required.

subject.description: The subject line, with {fact_name} placeholders for required facts only. One line. Up to 200 characters. Required.

blocks.description: The body, in order: paragraphs, a table of labelled rows, buttons. At least one, up to 40. Required.

type.description: What kind of block: paragraph (a paragraph of text), facts_table (labelled rows) or button (a link button). Required.

text.description: paragraph only: the words, with {fact_name} placeholders. `**bold**` marks bold in the HTML version. Up to 1000 characters.

plain.description: paragraph only, optional: different words for the plain-text version when they must differ from `text` (for example a colon where the HTML version has a button after it). Same placeholder rules. Up to 1000 characters.

show_if.description: Optional on a paragraph, a button and each table row: the name of a fact. The block or row appears only when that fact has a value. A placeholder for an optional fact is allowed only inside a block or row guarded by its own show_if.

label.description: button: the words on the button (no placeholders). On a table row: the left-hand label (no placeholders). Up to 80 characters.

link.description: button only: the address the button opens, normally a single placeholder such as {map_url}. Up to 200 characters.

plain_prefix.description: button only, optional: words put before the link in the plain-text version, for example Map: . Up to 40 characters.

has_fallback_line.description: button only, optional: when true the HTML version adds a line under the button that shows the address to copy if the button does not work. Absent means false.

rows.description: facts_table only: the rows, in order. At least one, up to 20.

label.description: The left-hand label of the row. No placeholders. Up to 80 characters.

value.description: The right-hand text, with {fact_name} placeholders. Up to 300 characters.

show_if.description: Optional: the name of a fact; the row appears only when that fact has a value.

is_active.description: The on/off switch. false means this message is not sent and the attempt is logged as not sent (no_template). Changing it does not make a new version. Required.

status.description: draft (being edited, never sent) or published (the version that may be sent). Set by the server.

version.description: 1 for the first published version, then one more each time a draft is published; a draft carries the number it will get. Set by the server.

previous_id.description: The published record this one replaces or was copied from. Absent on the first version. Set by the server.

published_at.description: When the draft was published (UTC); absent while a draft. Set by the server.

published_by.description: Who published it, as an actor string; absent while a draft. Set by the server.

id.description: UUID v4, set by the server; also the Firestore document id.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written under (currently 1). Set by the server.

created_at.description: When the record was created (UTC). Set by the server.

created_by.description: Who created it, as an actor string. Set by the server.

updated_at.description: When the record last changed (UTC). Set by the server.

updated_by.description: Who last changed it. Set by the server.

source.description: Where the record came from: dashboard or import. Set by the server.

deleted_at.description: When the record was soft deleted (UTC); absent while live. Set by the server.

deleted_by.description: Who soft deleted it. Set by the server.
